rationale: M65 MACRO RECOVERY. The analyzer publishes a `#define` from a `preproc_def`/`preproc_function_def` node (src/ast/real-cpp-analyzer.ts:3317). That branch is correct -- it published 1,277 macro symbols over a two-repo corpus. What it cannot do is mint a symbol for a node the grammar NEVER CREATED, and on real single-header libraries it does not create one for every directive. MEASURED (fmt 10.2.1 + nlohmann-json v3.11.3, 524 files, through the production entry): 3,483 `#define` lines in source vs 2,939 `preproc_def`/`preproc_function_def` nodes produced -- 544 macros the grammar never produced (15.6%), 543 of them in a file with >=1 ERROR node, and `calls` rows targeting those unpublished macros came to 9,004 of the 13,407 genuinely-unresolved targets (67%). `CHECK` alone is 6,734. The worst case is doctest.h: 672 `#define` lines, 131 `preproc_*` nodes, 2,627 ERROR nodes, one top-level ERROR span covering the WHOLE FILE (1-7107). THIS FIXTURE IS REAL CODE, NOT A CONSTRUCTION: it is a byte-for-byte copy of nlohmann/json's include/nlohmann/detail/abi_macros.hpp (3.8 KB, 22 `#define`s), the SMALLEST file in the corpus with a directive inside an ERROR span -- measured by walking every file, not guessed. The pinned fork produces 21 `preproc_*` nodes for its 22 defines: exactly one short. The missing one is `NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_END`, the LAST directive, because the ERROR region covers the file's final three lines. (In the original the ERROR span is 97-99 and the define is at 97; this copy is offset by its note.) THE CONTROL IS THE OTHER 21: they parse and publish through the EXISTING branch, so an implementation that deleted that branch, or that minted a symbol for every ALL-CAPS name it saw, fails here. Load-bearing assertions: (a) `expectSymbols` names NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_END with kind `macro` -- pinned by KIND and not only by name, so a phantom of another kind does not satisfy it; (b) `expectSymbolCount ... equals: 1` for it -- the only form that fails when the same name is minted twice, which is the collision the branch's own guard prevents; (c) NLOHMANN_JSON_VERSION_MAJOR (kind `constant`, an ordinary object-like define outside the ERROR region) must still be published -- the direction that costs real symbols; and (d) NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_BEGIN, the multi-line define immediately ABOVE the ERROR region, must be published with kind `constant` -- the grammar classifies it object-like, and an early draft of this fixture wrongly claimed `macro`, so this row also records that the ANALYZER was right and the fixture was wrong. WHY NOT A HAND-WRITTEN MINIMAL FILE: the first attempt at this fixture wrote a synthetic macro-decorated class to force an ERROR region, and the shape did NOT reproduce -- ERROR spans appeared but no `#define` fell inside one, so the fixture would have pinned nothing while reading as if it did. A fixture that cannot fail is worse than no fixture; it is the class the d6-blind-spot arm and the `retired: true` mutant records are about. UPSTREAM-FIX CASE: if the vendored fork is ever replaced by one that parses this shape cleanly, a `preproc_function_def` appears for line 97 and the ORDINARY branch publishes the same symbol, so name and kind are unchanged and these assertions still hold -- only the recovery arm stops being exercised. The mutant `cpp/macro-recovery-in-error-spans` is what proves the arm is live today.

expectSymbols.name: NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_END
expectSymbols.note: THE RECOVERED SYMBOL. `#define NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_END` is the LAST directive in this file (original line 97; line 157 in this copy, offset by the explanatory note above the library content). It falls inside the grammar's ERROR span, so no `preproc_function_def` node exists for it and the ordinary branch cannot publish it. The recovery arm reads the directive line and mints it. Pinned by KIND as well as name: a symbol of any other kind does not satisfy this row.

expectSymbols.name: NLOHMANN_JSON_VERSION_MAJOR
expectSymbols.note: THE CONTROL, and the direction that costs real symbols. An ordinary object-like `#define` outside any ERROR region: it parses and is published by the EXISTING branch. An implementation that deleted that branch to 'fix' the recovery case, or that only minted names it could not otherwise see, must still publish this.

expectSymbols.name: NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_BEGIN
expectSymbols.note: THE SHARPEST CONTROL, and it sits immediately ABOVE the ERROR region. It is itself a multi-line define, and the grammar classifies it OBJECT-LIKE (no parameter list), so the correct kind is `constant` -- an early draft of this fixture claimed `macro` and the ANALYZER WAS RIGHT and the fixture was wrong, which is the useful part of the record. A recovery arm that swept up every ALL-CAPS name in the file's neighbourhood, or that guessed function-like from 'looks like a macro', would mint it under a second conflicting kind and this row catches that.

expectSymbolCount.name: NLOHMANN_JSON_NAMESPACE_END
expectSymbolCount.note: THE ONLY ASSERTION FORM THAT FAILS ON A DUPLICATE. `expectSymbols` means 'at least one match', so a recovery arm that minted the same macro twice -- once from a stray preproc node and once from the directive line -- would satisfy it. `equals: 1` is what makes the branch's own collision guard (`!symbols.some(s => s.name === macroName)`) a tested invariant rather than a claim.
